The only dynamic element is the `source` array, which uses variable interpolation (`${pkgname}-${pkgver}.tar.gz::...`) to construct a fetch URL pointing to the project's own upstream GitHub tag. Variable expansion here produces a string—it does not execute any command, does not download anything, and does not write files. There are no command substitutions (`` `...` `` or `$((...))`), no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget`, and no top-level code that could exfiltrate data or run untrusted payloads.

Note: the `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` functions contain out-of-scope code for this gate (they will be audited later). Even there, the operations appear to be standard Go packaging (go mod download, go build with buildmode=pie and -trimpath), which is expected upstream behavior, not a supply-chain attack.
</details>
